text.p: Digital Biometrics Inc said Friday it is retroactively revising its financial results for the first quarter and full year of fiscal 1996 and the fourth quarter and full year of fiscal 1995 to comply with an accounting change issued by Securities and Exchange Commission.

On March 28, 1997 the SEC revised the accounting treatment for convertible securities with beneficial conversion features such as that contained in the company's convertible debenture issue of September, 1995.
As a result of the revision, the company is recognizing an additional $1,923,529 in interest expense in the first quarter of fiscal 1996, which ended on December 31, 1995.

The revised loss per share for the first quarter of fiscal 1996 is $0.39 per share, compared to the previously reported loss of $0.15 per share. The revised loss for the full year of fiscal 1996 is $1.24 per share compared to the previously reported loss of $1.03 per share.

The revisions to fiscal 1995 and 1996 financial statements have no impact on reported stockholders' equity or cash flows for any prior period presented, nor is there any impact on fiscal 1997 financial results.
There is no impact on the company's compliance with its covenants on its various lines of credit, the company said in a news release.

The convertible debenture issue of September, 1995 which gives rise to the revised Fiscal 1996 accounting treatment has been fully converted to common stock as of April, 1997, as previously announced by the Company.
The company noted that its prior accounting for the convertible debenture issue was and is consistent with generally accepted accounting principles.
Digital Biometrics makes and markets fingerprint identification and gaming products.
